instagram.caption:
Your business might already be listed in ChatGPT. Here's how to claim it, and the catch.
OpenAI opened Business Hub in beta on Nov 10. It's where you claim your business in ChatGPT and keep its info current.
The catch if you're local: OpenAI's help page says local stores and restaurants can only claim a listing that already exists, U.S. only for now.
1. Open Business Hub. OpenAI says it's in your ChatGPT sidebar. If it's not there, go to chatgpt.com/business-hub
2. Search your business name. Read the line under the box first: by continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms. They say OpenAI's AI assistant may call your business for its users (you can opt out), and you agree not to bring certain claims against OpenAI.
3. Prove it's yours. OpenAI lists a business phone, a business email, your website domain or Shopify.
4. Before any change goes live there's an identity check with Persona. Then OpenAI reviews it and emails you its decision.
We searched ours. Not listed. It offered to create one, which OpenAI says is for eligible online businesses.
Claiming it doesn't guarantee ChatGPT recommends you more. OpenAI says so itself.
Is your business in there yet?
Save this, and send it to whoever runs your Google listing.
Source: OpenAI, "Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT" (Nov 10, 2026); OpenAI Help Center, "Setting up your business on ChatGPT"; OpenAI, "Businesses in ChatGPT Terms". All read Nov 12, 2026. The Business Hub screens are from our own account.

#chatgpt #smallbusiness #contractor #localbusiness
